summary:
TerraTrace AI, developed by Team INNOVISION, is a global Earth observation and surface-change intelligence platform inspired by NASA's Space Apps Challenge theme, “Dancing with the SARs. Utilizes satellite data such as the NASA–ISRO NISAR data alongside Earth Observation data to identify areas of change.
There are 12 specific AI agents that can be used to detect different types of changes such as floods, deforestation, wildfires, glacial melt, subsidence, landslides, changes to agriculture and urban growth. You can choose the area you want to look at by using the coordinates, searching for a location or drawing a box on the map. The AI agents will then look at the data available and provide a unified report with evidence of what is happening.
TerraTrace AI is designed to help simplify the complex data from satellites and make Earth Observation more actionable. This allows users to monitor the environment, increase awareness of disasters, protect ecosystems and make more informed decisions.
details:
1. Project Overview

TerraTrace AI is a multi-agent artificial intelligence capable of identifying, analysing and interpreting changes in the environment on earth using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite data and earth observation data.

The idea for this project was inspired by NASA's earth observation capabilities and their NISAR mission with ISRO. This platform converts complex satellite observations into environmental intelligence. You can select any location on the interactive world map and it will automatically identify environmental changes for the chosen area. There is no need to manually select a disaster or environmental type.

This platform differs from other environmental monitoring platforms because it uses SAR observation. This means the observations can be carried out at any time of day and there is much less sensitivity to cloud.

2. How TerraTrace AI Works

The process is fully automated:

Select Location: Select an area on the interactive World Map.

Discovery: Discover relevant datasets in Earth Observation and extract any available satellite observations for your location and dates.

Sentinel-1 RTC Preprocessing: Process the data using VV and VH polarisations, converting to decibels.

Change Detection: Use temporal log ratio analysis to compare observations at different times, identifying possible changes in the environment.

AI Analysis: Identified changes undergo analysis by specialist AI agents using trained Machine Learning models to understand various environmental phenomena.

Multi Agent Orchestrator: An orchestrator is used to control the 12 specialist agents and collate results.

Visualisation: Visualise results using interactive maps, highlighted areas of change, evidence and AI explanations.

3. 12 Specialised AI Agents

The system has been designed to use 12 specialised AI agents which will identify specific environmental changes:

1. Flood Detection

This will identify any changes in SAR backscatter and water cover to identify any potential flood areas.

2. Wetland Monitoring

This will identify any changes in wetland area and water cover and surrounding land to identify any potential wetland issues.

3. Deforestation Monitoring

This will identify any issues within the forest, such as any changes in vegetation and potential deforestation.

4. Wildfire Monitoring

This will identify any changes in land surface radar to identify any potential burn areas.

5. Land Movement Monitoring

This will identify any potential land surface movement using appropriate radar sources.

6. Glacier Monitoring

This will identify any changes in glacier area, snow cover and land surface features relating to ice.

7. Landslide Detection

This will use changes from SAR and combine it with terrain information such as height and slope to identify any potential landslide areas.

8. Agriculture Monitoring

This will help identify any changes in agricultural land over time.

9. Urban Expansion Monitoring

This will identify any changes in built up land.

10. Mining Monitoring

This will identify any potential changes in land due to mining.

11. Coastal Monitoring

This will identify any changes in coastal areas, water boundaries and coastal land.

12. Unclassified Changes

This will look into changes that have been identified but are not confident they fit into the pre-defined environmental categories. This means we can look into the changes further.

Multi-Agent Orchestration

An overarching AI agent controls the 12 agents. It will control how the analysis is handled based on the location chosen by the user. It can decide what specific agents are needed and process their outputs to create a holistic view of the environmental data.

This means that TerraTrace can detect more than one environmental factor.

4. AI Model Training and NASA Earth Observation Data

TerraTrace is a classifier that uses features generated from satellite data to create Machine Learning Models that classify environmental changes.

Random Forest classifiers have been trained on these extracted features from Sentinel-1 RTC data, including VV/VH Backscatter measurements and temporal changes.

This pipeline includes extracting the features, creating the samples, training the classifier, validating and deploying it onto the appropriate agent.

The project includes using several sources of Earth Observation Data from NASA:

NASA Earthdata Search and CMR (Common Metadata Repository): This tool was used to search through and explore the available NASA Earth data.

NASA- ISRO NISAR: Key data source for this project. Advanced L/S Band SAR data will be integrated into the platform.

NASA UAVSAR: Additional SAR data from the air.

NASA GIBS: Enables global earth observation and provides map context using MODIS imagery.

Sentinel-1 RTC: Main source of SAR data. The processing and training pipeline has been implemented using this data. It provides ~10m resolution data with VV/VH polarizations.

Sentinel-2: Additional optical data.

Copernicus DEM: Provides elevation data. Contains slope data that is useful for landslide analysis.

The Random Forest training pipeline implemented has produced trained models for nine agents including Flood, Wetlands, Forest, Wildfire, Landslide, Urban, Mining, Coastal and Unclassified Change Detection.

The Ground Deformation, Glacier and Agricultural Activity agents are part of this 12 agent system. These agents require additional training and validation.

The data sources from NASA Earth Observation provide guidance for how to find, analyse and integrate data into the platform. The trained classifiers have been created using features from Sentinel-1 data.

  • Multi-agent orchestration

  • Image segmentation and classification

  • GeoPandas
  • NumPy
  • Geospatial vectorization
  • SAR backscatter analysis
  • Otsu thresholding

  • NASA–ISRO NISAR
  • NASA UAVSAR
  • NASA GIBS
  • Sentinel-1 RTC
  • Sentinel-2
  • Copernicus DEM

Data Access and Visualization

  • Microsoft Planetary Computer
  • Earth Search
  • Interactive global mapping
  • Geospatial visualization

6.) Benefits & Impact

TerraTrace AI provides a solution that makes high-end satellite technology easier to access for researchers, environmental groups, disaster management and decision makers.

Benefits include:

Early detection and investigation into potential environmental changes.

Better understanding of flood areas and vulnerable environmental areas.

Help monitor and protect forests.

Monitor changes in glaciers and coastal regions.

Detect disturbances in land due to mining, urban development and agriculture.

Observe worldwide environmental changes.

Interpretation of complicated SAR satellite data.

The platform will help analyse environmental factors with the detections indicating possible changes that need to be verified.

7.) Creativity & Innovation

The main innovation from this project is combining environmental change detection using SAR data with a well organised multi agent system.

Rather than having individual applications for each area such as floods, deforestation, glaciers, etc TerraTrace combines all these abilities into one global platform.

This has been done using 12 specialised agents meaning we have a very modular system where individual changes can be investigated and the results put together by the orchestrator.

An important factor was using multi temporal radar data. This allows us to compare data acquired at different times to investigate any changes.

The project was inspired by NASA’s Earth observation ecosystem and NISAR mission to show how we can combine advanced satellite technology, machine learning and geospatial intelligence to overcome issues facing the global environment.

8.) Considerations

When designing the project we took into consideration:

Scientific accuracy – Using actual satellite data and scientifically accurate methods.

Data availability – Taking into account where data is available, when it was taken, the resolution and polarisation.

Model accuracy – Using training and validation, making sure we aren’t classifying environmental changes without support.

SAR Accuracy – Considering any effects from the terrain, noise, surface and seasonality.

Worldwide – Making sure the platform can be used globally.

Interpretability – Providing visualisations of the changes detected with satellite data to explain what has happened.

Extensible – The specialised agents can be expanded to include more data sets, algorithms and trained models as the platform progresses.

9. Conclusion

This project seeks to tackle the challenge of taking complex earth observation data and turning it into useful information.

With a combination of SAR satellite data, machine learning and geospatial processing, we aim to create a new way to understand environmental changes.

We hope to make these observations more usable by turning them into useful information to help people understand and protect the environment.
